findings.claim: The write verbs (claims submit, checks try, checks submit, judge) pick their store by `--path`, "the repository whose store to use", defaulting to the current directory. After this plan the repository root means the `.okf` namespace, so an agent that runs `kmaudit claims todo docs/guide.md` and then `kmaudit claims submit -` (as kmctl-claims-extractor and kmctl-check-writer do) sends docs answers to the `.okf` store, where they are refused or, for a concept id both folders share, matched against the wrong section. The plan never says how a submit names its namespace (`--path docs`, the namespace carried in the answer, or another rule), and the agents and skills in apm/.apm that call these verbs are not in any outcome's touches. The "It worked when" test only exercises todo, so the docs workflow can pass review and still not work end to end.

The rule that maps a path to a namespace is undefined for a file or a subfolder. A plain folder has no marker (an OKF bundle has index.md with okf_version), and the namespace is "that folder's path", so `kmaudit claims todo docs/sub/page.md` or `kmaudit claims todo docs/sub` can name `docs/sub`, a second store that overlaps `docs` and splits its answers silently. The agents call todo with one FILE at a time, so this path is the common one. The plan needs to state the rule (for example the nearest folder above the file that already has a store, else the top folder under the repository root) before resolve_target is rewritten.

The O1/O2 facts do not match the prose. O1 (behaviour, needs none) accepts any folder, but without O2 every folder still writes the one .kmctl/audit.sqlite, and concept ids are relative to the folder, so docs/guide.md and .okf/guide.md both give `guide#...` section ids in one store: shipping O1 alone causes exactly the clash P2 names. The dependency runs the other way (O1 needs O2; O2 can ship with `.okf` as the only namespace). Also, O1's checked-by ("a check never reads a file in the audited folder") and the prose's 12 Repository call sites in check_verbs.py, ui.py and coverage.py belong to O1's fix of P1, yet those files are listed only under O2, which fixes P2. plan.split would cut on these facts and produce a first ticket that cannot meet its own check.

Every writing verb now names its namespace by --path FOLDER, todo --json prints the namespace and a Next step with --path, and the agents, skills, README and commands.md are in O3's touches, checked by r2 and r9.

The plan now states the mapping rule (a path inside an existing namespace narrows it and opens no store; an OKF bundle's files mean the bundle; a folder holding a namespace is refused naming it; the root holding .okf means .okf), checked by r2b and r6.

O1 is now the per-namespace store and mapping (support, needs none) and O2 the plain-folder audit (behaviour, needs O1) holding the steps.py Repository change, so a split cannot ship the folder change before the store split.
